CR-20260909-skills / CR-20260909-display-screen (DEC-015): skill-generated HTML is rendered in an <iframe srcdoc> WITHOUT a sandbox attribute. Same-origin scripts in that HTML can read localStorage and call same-origin APIs (e.g. DELETE /api/providers/[id]). The user (2026-09-09, msg 54-1) accepted this risk for the local single-admin form; the only mitigation is the non-dismissible notice bar (REQ-F-025 ②). Sandboxing the iframe is a mandatory exit obligation for a future CR. SCOPE EXPANDED by CR-20260910-agent-tooling (see sibling entry skill-html-unsandboxed-web-source).

CR-20260910-agent-tooling (CP-20, 单向门; R1 架构角色提出): REQ-F-034 read_url lets attacker-controlled web page content enter the model's context. That content can instruct the model to call save_insight(html), placing attacker-authored HTML into the SAME unsandboxed same-origin <iframe srcdoc> covered by skill-html-unsandboxed. DEC-015's accepted-risk premise was 'the user dragged in a poisoned skill folder' — a source the user chose and trusts. This CR widens the source to ANY web page reachable by search, so the premise no longer holds and the trust surface is strictly larger. Attack chain: user question -> web_search -> read_url on attacker page -> prompt injection in page body -> model calls save_insight ->攻击者 HTML renders with same-origin script access (localStorage, DELETE /api/providers/[id]). The user was shown this chain and the three options (A: make 联网 and save_insight mutually exclusive; B: sandbox the iframe first; C: accept) and chose C — explicitly accepting the expanded risk (2026-09-10, R1 人工终裁 item 3). Mitigation remains only the non-dismissible notice bar (REQ-F-025 ②). Detection route is '发现不了' for the injection path itself, which is why CP-20 is registered as a 单向门 per DEC-021 ②. Sandboxing the iframe stays a mandatory exit obligation for a future CR and is now higher priority than before this CR.

Intermittent 'Failed to fetch' was investigated on 2026-09-12 and traced to the machine running at ~90% memory, not to a defect: 600 requests succeeded with zero failures, 1,200 requests moved RSS by 1 MB, and there are no crash records. The largest single consumer on that machine was Claude Code itself (17 processes, ~2 GB) — the investigator, not Jarvis (656 MB). CR-20260912-runtime-visibility makes the consequence visible and recoverable; it does NOT fix the cause. Freeing memory remains the highest-value step and needs no code change.

BUDGET_SHARES remains internally inconsistent by design after CR-20260912-context-degrade: singleToolResult (0.15) x 4 equals totalInput (0.6), so four full-sized tool results still exhaust the whole input allowance by construction. The CR absorbs the consequence by tightening progressively rather than refusing the turn; it does NOT change the declared shares, because that would shorten every tool output and has a far wider blast radius. TEST-190 ① pins the inequality so the next person to touch the shares sees it. Also recorded honestly: CR-20260912-sandbox-and-budget widened the gap by 60% when it replaced the constant 12,000 cap with 0.15 of the real window — that change was correct on its own terms, and it made this failure more likely.

The multi-agent-insight-reviewer skill is 167,755 characters across twenty reference files against a 32KB injection cap and an 8,000-token read_skill cap, so roughly four fifths of it never reaches the model. CR-20260912-skill-report-bridge does not change that ratio. Also unresolved: the report column and the chat console still share one centre axis and overlap by 78% at 1440x900; the CR works around the default state by collapsing the console once a report lands, but a user who manually expands it still has the report covered.

CR-20260912-skill-paging makes a large skill fully reachable, but two limits stay. The manifest is ordered by path, not by relevance, so the model decides what to read from filenames and sizes alone. And the report column still shares one centre axis with the chat console: this CR only lowered the step-stream height cap from 75vh to 58vh so the top of a report stays legible, and a user who manually expands the console still has most of the report covered. Resolving that needs the two to occupy different horizontal regions, which is a larger layout change.

CR-20260912-reading-lane was built on a misread requirement and has been reverted in full. The user's ruling 「报告不用跟着位移」 meant 'leave the console position alone, and the report need not move for it' — i.e. keep things as they are. It was read as 'separate them horizontally, but keep the report fixed', which is the opposite. The user corrected it: 「我说了不修改对话框位置。还是底下居中，展开后可以遮挡报告内容，因为展开意味着需要对话。」 Everything that CR introduced (REQ-F-160, DEC-140, TASK-220, TEST-220, and its revisions to REQ-F-002, REQ-F-090 ①, ui-contract LB-02 and the in-iframe breakpoint) is rolled back; code and specs are back to the state before it. The user's reasoning is worth keeping on its own: expanding the console IS the signal that the user wants to converse rather than read, so covering the report at that moment is correct behaviour, not a defect. That premise invalidates the 'overlap = problem' assumption behind the preceding CRs' framing — the mitigations they shipped (auto-collapse on report, 58vh step-stream cap) remain, and were not objected to.
